parser-parse.title: How Parser::parse works (clap derive)
parser-parse.description: Parses the real command line into your struct; on bad input it prints the error and exits.

slides.caption: The derive turns struct fields into arguments: #[arg(long)] makes --name. Option fields are optional.
clap reads std::env::args(): here just the program name.
--name was not given, so the Option is None.

parser-parse-from.title: How Parser::parse_from works (clap derive)
parser-parse-from.description: Parses a given list of arguments; the first one is the program name.

slides.caption: Exits the process on errors, like parse().

parser-try-parse-from.title: How Parser::try_parse_from works (clap derive)
parser-try-parse-from.description: Like parse_from, but returns Err instead of exiting.

slides.caption: Fields without a default or Option are required. Errors come back as clap::Error.
The Err tells you what went wrong.
e.exit() prints the usual message and exits with code 2.

parser-try-parse.title: How Parser::try_parse works (clap derive)
parser-try-parse.description: Parses the real command line, returning Err instead of exiting.

slides.caption: Useful to log or translate errors before exiting.

command-new.title: How Command::new works
command-new.description: Starts building a command line interface with a program name.

slides.caption: Command describes the program: its name, arguments and subcommands. It does not read anything yet.

command-arg.title: How Command::arg works
command-arg.description: Adds one argument to the command.

slides.caption: A plain Arg::new is a positional argument.

command-about.title: How Command::about works
command-about.description: Sets the one-line description shown in --help.

slides.caption: long_about adds a longer text for --help.
With derive, the doc comment is used.

command-subcommand.title: How Command::subcommand works
command-subcommand.description: Adds a subcommand, like git commit or cargo build.

slides.caption: A subcommand has its own arguments. After parsing, ask which subcommand was used.
Its arguments are parsed with its own matches.

command-get-matches-from.title: How Command::get_matches_from works
command-get-matches-from.description: Parses the given arguments; on error, prints it and exits.

slides.caption: get_matches() reads the real command line.

command-try-get-matches-from.title: How Command::try_get_matches_from works
command-try-get-matches-from.description: Parses the given arguments and returns Result<ArgMatches, Error>.

slides.caption: Nothing is printed and the process keeps running.

command-arg-required-else-help.title: How Command::arg_required_else_help works
command-arg-required-else-help.description: Shows help instead of running when no arguments are given.

slides.caption: Reported as the error kind DisplayHelpOnMissingArgumentOrSubcommand.
Good for tools that do nothing useful without input.

command-subcommand-required.title: How Command::subcommand_required works
command-subcommand-required.description: Makes it an error to omit the subcommand.

slides.caption: Combine with arg_required_else_help(true) to show help instead.

command-render-help.title: How Command::render_help works
command-render-help.description: The help text as a value, without printing or exiting.

slides.caption: Used in usage lines and errors.
get_bin_name is the name actually invoked.

arg-new.title: How Arg::new works
arg-new.description: Creates an argument with an id (the name you use to read it back).

slides.caption: With derive, the field name is the id.
Combine with short for both forms.

arg-help.title: How Arg::help works
arg-help.description: The description of the argument in --help.

slides.caption: With derive, the field's doc comment.
Positional arguments are optional unless required.
With derive: non-Option fields are required.

arg-default-value.title: How Arg::default_value works
arg-default-value.description: The value used when the argument is not given.

slides.caption: With a default, get_one always returns Some.
value_source() tells you which one you got.

arg-action.title: How Arg::action works
arg-action.description: Says what to do when the argument appears: store a value, set a flag, count, append...

slides.caption: Flags without values need an action like SetTrue or Count; options store values by default.
Read Count with get_count, SetTrue with get_flag, Append with get_many.

arg-value-parser.title: How Arg::value_parser works
arg-value-parser.description: Parses and validates the value into a type.

arg-num-args.title: How Arg::num_args works
arg-num-args.description: How many values one occurrence takes, like 1..=3.

slides.caption: Take values until the next flag.

arg-value-name.title: How Arg::value_name works
arg-value-name.description: The placeholder for the value in help, like <FILE>.

slides.caption: ArgGroup with multiple(false) does the same for many.

arg-requires.title: How Arg::requires works
arg-requires.description: If this argument is given, another one must be too.

slides.caption: Only checked when this argument is present.

arg-env.title: How Arg::env works
arg-env.description: Reads the value from an environment variable when it is not on the command line.

slides.caption: Needs the "env" feature. The command line wins over the variable.
Aliases are not listed in help; visible_alias is.

arg-global.title: How Arg::global works
arg-global.description: Makes an argument usable after any subcommand too.

slides.caption: The value is propagated to every level.

arggroup-new.title: How ArgGroup::new works
arggroup-new.description: Groups arguments, for "exactly one of" or "at least one of" rules.

slides.caption: By default at most one member may be given.

matches-get-one.title: How ArgMatches::get_one works
matches-get-one.description: The value of an argument, as the type its value_parser produced.

slides.caption: The type must match the value parser (String by default), or it panics.
Return a reference to the parsed value.
None if it was not given and has no default.

matches-get-flag.title: How ArgMatches::get_flag works
matches-get-flag.description: Whether a SetTrue/SetFalse flag is on.

slides.caption: Panics if the argument is not a flag.

matches-get-many.title: How ArgMatches::get_many works
matches-get-many.description: All values of an argument, as an iterator.

matches-get-count.title: How ArgMatches::get_count works
matches-get-count.description: How many times a Count flag was given.

matches-contains-id.title: How ArgMatches::contains_id works
matches-contains-id.description: true if the argument has a value (given or defaulted).

slides.caption: Defaults count as present; check value_source to tell them apart.

matches-subcommand.title: How ArgMatches::subcommand works
matches-subcommand.description: The used subcommand's name and matches, if any.

slides.caption: The usual way to branch on subcommands.

matches-subcommand-name.title: How ArgMatches::subcommand_name works
matches-subcommand-name.description: The name of the subcommand used, if any.

slides.caption: None when no subcommand was given.

matches-subcommand-matches.title: How ArgMatches::subcommand_matches works
matches-subcommand-matches.description: The matches of a named subcommand, if it was used.

slides.caption: None if another (or no) subcommand was used.

matches-value-source.title: How ArgMatches::value_source works
matches-value-source.description: Where a value came from: command line, environment or default.

slides.caption: CommandLine and EnvVariable are the others.

matches-remove-one.title: How ArgMatches::remove_one works
matches-remove-one.description: Takes the value out of the matches (owned, no clone).

error-kind.title: How clap::Error::kind works
error-kind.description: What kind of parse error happened.

error-render.title: How clap::Error::render works
error-render.description: The full error message as text, without printing it.

slides.caption: exit() would print it and end the process.

error-exit-code.title: How clap::Error::exit_code works
error-exit-code.description: The process exit code exit() would use.

slides.caption: Usage errors exit with 2, help and version with 0.
Match it if you handle errors yourself.
